excerpt: Ubuntu is a primary platform for all major IDEs, game development tools, and AI/ML software.
Each release of Ubuntu delivers the latest applications, libraries, and toolchains.

The power of a full Ubuntu terminal environment on Windows with Windows Subsystem for Linux. Streamline web application development, run cutting-edge AI/ML tooling, develop cross-platform applications, and manage IT infrastructure
Ubuntu Desktop is also certified on the Raspberry Pi, delivering a rich developer experience on this powerful Arm device.
It's easy to install in place of Windows, or run Ubuntu alongside it.
Ubuntu offers essential applications for web browsing, messaging, gaming, and content creation, including Firefox, Chrome, Discord, Steam, and OBS Studio, supporting all your daily computing needs.
As a lightweight and highly efficient operating system, installing Ubuntu on older hardware can improve performance and extend the lifespan of your devices.
Anyone can use Ubuntu Pro for free on up to 5 machines
Experience Ubuntu with different choices of default desktop environment, applications and settings, backed by the full Ubuntu archive for packages and updates.

Unity just felt consistent, usable and boring - all qualities that I appreciate in a desktop environment... some of my devices still use XFCE and there's almost nothing that I find lacking in that regard.
Unity was probably the most straightforward n00b-friendly Linux DE. I'm still rocking it in 2022... It's less objectionable than GNOME and less fiddly than KDE.
For me the killer feature of Unity is the HUD allowing you to simply type to find menu items. Save so much time going through options it is incredible.

Canonical had at some point two variants of Unity, the regulate one (slow) and a qml based one (super snappy). I'm still sad that they did not stick with the qml version. GNOME nowerdays is fine, but for years it was slow and lacking compared to what we already had with qml Unity.

Unity's global menu system was wonderful... switching to gnome was like going back 10 years. Seeing multiple empty bars across the screen makes it completely unusable to me... I'm using kde plasma now with a global menu set up. It's good but isn't as hassle free as Unity was.
The best feature from Unity was just tapping alt and easily finding the menu option on the app I was running. This helped a lot with apps that had many or deep menu items like GIMP or LibreOffice.

I have never understood unity. For all it's faults and annoyances I have never once considered gnome, kde, or even cinnamon inferior to unity... any features unity had a claim to fame for were implemented and then superseded by gnome a long time ago.

I still use Gnome metacity flashback because it wastes less screen space and has a nice virtual workspace switcher. I'm less happy with the configuration/tweak tools and the fact that they are only accessible from within the account and the display itself.
Compiz kick started the belief that Linux 'Year of the Desktop' could be a real thing. Wobbly windows, fire and the cube were great demos to get people interested in Linux.

I've been using Ubuntu/Compiz for a couple years and it has some annoying quirks e.g. child windows that pop up on the wrong monitor! (thank goodness for WIN+SHIFT+arrow keys!!) But... I have NO desire to go back to Win(10/8) horrible user/developer experience.
Unfortunately, Compiz seems not to be actively maintained since 2016. It looks like the development is suddenly stopped... I'm kinda wondering what happened to them.

I used Compiz with 17.04 and it was nice, but I decided to give a shot at the native Gnome with 18.04 when I reinstalled from scratch. To be honest, it's not perfect but it does the job. So I will stick with it.

I still remember when Gnome 2 reached its peak with Ubuntu in the early 2000's. It was pretty much the complete, reliable, configurable, and robust desktop that Linux ever needed. Anything since that has been a downhill.
To each their own, but I really don't like the Compiz style of window managers. I have better things to watch than my windows moving around.

This is interesting, but not compelling. I want: 1) Better video drivers. 2) An option to Dual-boot with another OS. 3) To remove the painful Unity interface. 4) More titles to play... it's hard to convince myself to buy this.
Too bad the hardware is overpriced... Reflects bad on Ubuntu.
Don't bother. They want you to use proprietary driver blobs without any source code for them.

I have but one humble wish: when I want to start the calculator app I open the Dash and type 'calc'. However for some reason LibreOffice Calc has higher priority than the Calculator app, so I always have to select it specifically instead of just pressing Enter.

Caveat.. not a ubuntu user here per se... But left because of some of the bloatware/opinonated stuff and it crashed a lot. Plus I like Antergos with i3-gnome better than anything I've ever used before... Much better performance, less crashes/bugs.
Ubuntu works for me and my wife and has for years. I pine for the days of Gnome 2 but that's not coming back. If Unity could be made into Gnome 2 but keep Unity people happy then that would be cool.
